TabPage, BookPage, player, History, records_screen, and gallery use the migrated status representation. Consumers do not compare message strings or maintain duplicate notice lifetime state.

The ticket remains in progress. Integration, acceptance, hardening, and closure remain with the parent.
findings: F1: preserving genuine current errors is incomplete for actions initiated from Recently Listened and History.
F2: obsolete-source rejection does not cover every notice writer.
F3: obsolete-source rejection introduces inconsistent playback state.
gaps: The three findings need behavioral regression evidence before handoff.
Android inspection remains explicitly excluded under t1-dth0. Host geometry tests and the layout scan do not establish Android visual acceptance.

The retained whitespace check names implementation commit 3903711325358a4b95a9b28d9f0e19d475b74323. The later documentation-only commit was inspected, but no retained whitespace execution names the final review HEAD.

evidence: Playback remains the state owner. PlaybackStatus and PlaybackActionNotice are immutable interface payloads; messagesFor owns display scope; RecordSaveStatus owns retry callbacks; RecordSaveNotice remains a pure view.
Action failure, record recovery, and pending-save failure have distinct lifetimes. Save failure derives from existing account write state instead of duplicating it in message text.
The scoped query and shared notice widget serve multiple real consumers without speculative extension points. Public documentation explains account, book, and edition scope.

API assessment: scope selection provides useful granularity; consumers need no redundant filtering; status subscriptions keep coupling narrow; views retain no second notice state; actions flow through controllers.

All notice writers were traced. Source validity is still coordinated separately in _open, _restorePosition, and _audioFailed; _actionFailed accepts only an edition identifier and cannot enforce that invariant.
No performance measurements were run or inferred. The review makes no new speed claim.
findings: F2: User and Ousterhout — source-validity knowledge is spread across writers rather than enforced by the notice transition. Adding or changing an asynchronous failure path requires coordinating its checks with the other writers.
F3: User and Ousterhout — the decision to suppress a notice also suppresses the state transition that reconciles Playback with an already-paused decoder.
gaps: The documented notice invariant checks for a signed-in account, but does not establish that a notice still describes the source that caused it.
No runtime reproduction is claimed for the design findings; their evidence is the ownership and coordination visible in the source.

findings.trigger: Unexecuted reproduction: retain listening history for book B, open book A, remove B's downloaded file, then tap Resume B in Recently Listened. A corresponding case is restoring B from all-book History with nothing open.
findings.expected: The failed action has a visible explanation associated with B, while A's player content and unrelated surfaces remain free of B's error.
findings.observedOrPredicted: The action notice is stored, but no relevant visible surface displays it. The player selects A's edition; Recently Listened rows have no notice input; the nothing-open player requests only account notices. History closes before restoration and can open the retained or empty player after failure.
findings.evidence: PlayerView._resume calls Playback.open at screen.dart:189. The stage filters notices to the retained edition at screen.dart:324. Recently Listened is wired at screen.dart:197 and :412; recent.dart:94-148 renders rows without notices. timeline.dart:156-164 and :186-189 close/navigate without an outcome-specific failure presentation. Existing widget tests check unrelated History visibility, not a failed History action.
findings.proposedFix: Connect these initiating surfaces to Playback-owned scoped notices, showing the failure beside the attempted book or in a book-labelled action surface. Preserve the existing scope query and controller boundaries. Add widget regressions through Resume and History callbacks.

findings.trigger: Unexecuted reproduction: keep A open, begin restoring a saved position in B, hold B's local-file lookup, refresh the same account with unchanged A and replacement files under B's existing edition identifier, then release the old lookup with no file.
findings.expected: The obsolete lookup result must not publish a download error against replacement B.
findings.observedOrPredicted: _restorePosition checks only the account generation after the wait and publishes a notice using B's identifier. The same-account refresh leaves that generation unchanged, so messagesFor displays the old source's failure on replacement B. Already-published notices can likewise survive a same-account replacement of a non-open edition because the notice retains no source identity and bind does not invalidate it.
findings.evidence: playback.dart:791-809 retains the original edition across _savedFiles but checks only generation. bind at :1135-1180 can replace B while retaining unchanged A without advancing generation. _actionFailed at :2115 stores only editionId, operation, and message; messagesFor at :211-216 matches edition identifiers. In contrast, _open rechecks _bound after its lookup and _audioFailed checks _sameEdition.
findings.proposedFix: Make Playback's notice transition retain and validate the originating account/source context for every asynchronous failure path. Reconcile existing notices when library sources change. Cover both a delayed restore result and an already-published notice followed by source replacement.
findings.designSource: User: one owner for invariant-preserving transitions and one model for existing/new behavior. Ousterhout: hide source-validity decisions instead of requiring each writer to repeat them. The concrete maintenance cost is coordinating _open, _restorePosition, _audioFailed, and bind whenever source-validity rules change.

findings.trigger: Unexecuted reproduction: play A, begin opening downloaded B with its engine load held, refresh the same account with unchanged A and a replacement source for B, then fail the held old-B load.
findings.expected: Suppress the obsolete B notice, but leave Playback's playing/active state consistent with the stopped decoder.
findings.observedOrPredicted: _audioFailed pauses the engine and then returns on the source mismatch before clearing playing and active. During the failed open, decoder samples are ignored because _decoderReady is false. Playback can therefore continue reporting that A is playing although the engine is stopped.
findings.evidence: playback.dart:1503-1513 disables decoder acceptance before pausing/loading. _accept at :1570 rejects samples while loading or not decoder-ready. _audioFailed pauses at :1113, returns at :1123, and skips state reconciliation at :1126-1132. The existing obsolete-source regression checks an initially empty player, so it cannot expose retained playing state.
findings.proposedFix: Separate notice eligibility from failure cleanup. Within the still-current account, reconcile playback state after the engine pause even when the attempted source is obsolete; suppress only the obsolete notice. Add a held-load regression starting with another edition actively playing.
findings.designSource: User: orchestration must keep related state coherent behind one transition. Ousterhout: keep distinct decisions separate. Notice eligibility currently controls decoder-state cleanup, so changing source filtering can silently change playback lifecycle behavior.
